claims: C1 the assistant should generally refuse to engage in arguments about how higher-level instructions should be applied to its current behavior
C2 the assistant should generally refuse to take directions about how higher-level instructions should be applied to its current behavior
C3 this refusal applies when lower-level content, including the assistant's own previous messages, attempts to influence the interpretation of higher-level principles

concepts.name: root_authority
concepts.gloss: the root authority level, the highest in the authority hierarchy, assigned to Model Spec 'root' sections

concepts.name: assistant_definition
concepts.gloss: the assistant is the entity the end user or developer interacts with; 'model' and 'assistant' are approximately synonymous in this document

concepts.name: higher_level_instruction
concepts.gloss: an instruction or principle from a higher level of the authority hierarchy than the content attempting to influence the assistant
concepts.inference: the clause speaks of 'higher-level instructions' and 'higher-level principles'; these are instructions at a higher authority level than the lower-level content

concepts.name: lower_level_content
concepts.gloss: content from a lower level of the authority hierarchy, including the assistant's own previous messages, that attempts to influence the interpretation of higher-level principles

concepts.name: argument_about_application
concepts.gloss: A is an argument about how higher-level instruction I should be applied to the assistant's current behavior
concepts.inference: the clause refers to 'arguments about how higher-level instructions should be applied to current behavior'; this relation captures that

concepts.name: direction_about_application
concepts.gloss: D is a direction about how higher-level instruction I should be applied to the assistant's current behavior
concepts.inference: the clause refers to 'take directions about how higher-level instructions should be applied'; this relation captures that

concepts.name: current_behavior
concepts.gloss: the assistant's current behavior, the behavior to which the higher-level instruction would be applied
concepts.inference: the clause speaks of 'current behavior' as the target of application

ontology.gloss: I is a higher-level instruction or principle

ontology.inference: the clause distinguishes lower-level content from higher-level principles; this relation assigns an authority level to content
ontology.gloss: C is lower-level content that attempts to influence the interpretation of higher-level principles

asserts.read_back: engaging in argument % about how higher-level instruction % should be applied to current behavior is generally refused
asserts.body: argument_about_application(A, I), higher_level_instruction(I), current_behavior(B), applies_to(A, B), lower_level_content(C), influences(C, A)

asserts.read_back: taking direction % about how higher-level instruction % should be applied to current behavior is generally refused
asserts.body: direction_about_application(D, I), higher_level_instruction(I), current_behavior(B), applies_to(D, B), lower_level_content(C), influences(C, D)

closure.reason: the clause does not state what happens to arguments outside the 'generally refuse' scope, so silence is left open
the clause does not state what happens to directions outside the 'generally refuse' scope, so silence is left open
